subject.title: fix(agents): prevent duplicate subagent recovery after restart

question: Should the canonical fix serialize the entire orphan-recovery scheduler as this PR does, or enforce a per-session in-flight claim and fresh store check as proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103823?
rationale: Both approaches plausibly stop duplicate resume turns but alter different ownership boundaries and retry/coalescing semantics; selecting the permanent session-recovery invariant requires maintainer judgment beyond automated correctness review.

options.title: Prefer the per-session boundary
options.body: Use a claim immediately around the final store check and resume dispatch so the invariant remains protected across all current and future scan callers without globally serializing unrelated recovery work.

options.title: Adopt scheduler single-flight
options.body: Keep this PR's coalesced scheduler after real restart proof demonstrates that queued requests, retries, and distinct active-run views remain correct.

recommendation.title: Prefer the per-session boundary
recommendation.body: Use a claim immediately around the final store check and resume dispatch so the invariant remains protected across all current and future scan callers without globally serializing unrelated recovery work.

likelyOwner.reason: The orphan-recovery mechanism appears to originate from this person's merged implementation, making them the strongest available history-based owner for its concurrency contract.
